gen-dafont-nordic-gf-gafata: Nordic looks ancient and powerful, its monoweight strokes spaced out like brush dabs on paper. And Gafata, a plain sans with a wide-eyed e, brings a contemporary, businesslike steadiness underneath.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-geist: Cramped, closed letters with a monoweight stroke give Nordic its ancient, brush-dabbed force. Geist follows with wide-open forms and a level beat, so paragraphs of it settle into solid, unspiky blocks of text.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-gidole: Ancient and blunt, Nordic keeps its letters closed up tight and spaced like brush dabs, while Gidole's terminals stay apart like open scissor blades. Nordic supplies the weight; Gidole, drawn like neon tube, lightens everything around it.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-golos-text: Weathered, forceful letters set the scene in Nordic, each one closed up and drawn in a single monoweight stroke. And Golos Text, with its large x-height and widely parted s, opens the page right back up.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-heebo: Heebo reads with a lofty middle band and curves that stop short instead of closing in. Then Nordic comes in, ancient and powerful, its cramped, closed letters giving that openness something solid to push against.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-hind-guntur: Nordic brings ancient power, spaced like brush dabs and cramped shut like a pressed leaf fold. And Hind Guntur, a sans-serif with stamped-metal lowercase and wide gaps at its curve ends, wants a generous size so those openings can breathe.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-hind-mysuru: Contemporary, with lowercase pressing up toward the ascender line. Nordic's closed, ancient letters meet Hind Mysuru's ajar-mouthed a, and that gap between shut and open is the strongest thing the pair has going.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-huninn: Huninn keeps its s terminals clear of the body and its crossbars as fat as the stems they join. Huninn's open, modern letters then stand against Nordic's cramped, ancient ones, which feel weighty and brush-dabbed by comparison.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-karla: Approachable and a bit stocky, Karla has a gaping c and a deep middle band. Nordic, ancient and powerful in closed monoweight strokes, belongs on the heading, kept to a few big words, while Karla carries everything else.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-kedebideri: Kedebideri reads open and friendly, its rounded letters rising to a skyward x-height. Nordic sits above with its cramped, closed forms and brush-dab spacing, giving the page an ancient, powerful weight that the sans then relaxes.
